summary: Exam-bypass tool scrapes foreground-window text and ships browser session cookies through an author-controlled relay
details: Package presents itself as a 'Windows Diagnostic Utility' but is a stealth exam-bypass client. main.js line 314 POSTs foreground-window text (scraped via bundled UI Automation binaries bin/uia_extract.exe / uia_extract.py, explicitly targeting Safe Exam Browser and code editors) to a hardcoded Cloudflare Worker at https://ai-script.test0ing7.workers.dev; the caller cannot reconfigure the destination. config.json ships two base64-encoded third-party Groq API keys (gsk_...) that the runtime decodes and uses to authenticate the relay calls. bin/chrome_cookies.ps1 is a ready-to-run Chrome/Edge/Brave cookie stealer that copies the Cookies SQLite databases, DPAPI-unwraps the os_crypt key, AES-GCM-decrypts cookie values, and emits session cookies for.openai.com,.chatgpt.com, auth0.openai.com, and auth.openai.com. bin/kalamasha-tool.js copies electron.exe to SearchApp.exe, spawns it detached with windowsHide, and installs a watchdog that respawns the process on exit to resist termination; main.js applies SetWindowDisplayAffinity 0x11 to hide the overlay from screen capture and sets process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0' to bypass TLS-inspecting proxies. Cover-story (diagnostic utility) does not match the shipped behavior (foreground-window content exfiltration to an author relay plus a browser session-cookie stealer targeting OpenAI/ChatGPT).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
